text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) confirmed on Wednesday that it has made a block sale of shares on the Budapest bourse in Hungarian home products maker Graboplast.

The EBRD said the sale on Tuesday of 120,000 shares, or about 40 percent of its holding in Graboplast, was its first through normal channels on a bourse in central Europe and had gone well enough to warrant further sales through stock markets.

"It was a transaction that we initiated because we felt that the price was right and the demand was there," said Gyorgy Karady, director of the EBRD's Hungary Team in London. "It was a transaction that was part of our normal portfolio management activities for listed securities."

"I was very pleased with the way it went. In fact it was the first time the EBRD has done such a sale that performed a partial exit from a portfolio company anywhere in central Europe through one of the markets," Karady added.

"This was the first and I'm sure it will not be the last because...it is part of our portfolio management strategy in central Europe for listed companies so we will do similar things elsewhere when the opportunity arises."
Karady said the transaction was handled by Creditanstalt Securities. The trade was made at 4,720 forints per share, slightly below Graboplast's Tuesday closing price of 4750 forints.

Karady said the sale was in no way a sign of lack of confidence in Graboplast, which is one of Hungary's leading makers of home improvement products and has a share capitalisation of more than four billion forints.

"It's quite the opposite, It's a reflection of our total conviction that Graboplast is an excellent company," Karady said. "We are retaining the bulk of our stake and we will remain investors in the company."
The EBRD has invested millions of dollars in Hungary and other central and east European countries to bolster privatisation.
"I was very pleased that the Budapest Stock Exchange had the liquidity to perform such large sales without putting any pressure on the price because in fact the price rose," Karady added.

"It means that the Budapest Stock Exchange is a credible mechanism for privatising companies and then subsequently the investors finding their exits. It's a credible exit route and not what some people have said in the past that listing on a stock exchange may not be a credible exit route."
